messages:
maria: seeing a spike in outbound failures from edge-np-eu-west1 starting ~08:12 UTC. model pulls to registry.gcr.io and calls to our metrics sink are timing out. :eyes:
joel: any recent egress policy changes?
ankit: rolled the new envoy egress-policy yesterday to tighten host-based allowlists, but I scoped it to the mesh egress filter only — shouldn't touch SNAT/conntrack.
maria: logs show lots of `ICMP destination unreachable` and `tcp reset` in envoy logs. also `conntrack: table full` in kernel syslog on a few nodes. snippet: ```kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet```.
olivia: that sounds like conntrack exhaustion, often from SNAT port churn when sidecars proxy many outbound flows. did we change any iptables nat rules?
ankit: I added a `PREROUTING` rule in the mesh to redirect 0.0.0.0/0:443 -> envoy, plus an egress-gateway for specific hosts. maybe the redirect is bypassing the existing SNAT pool.
joel: can you run `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` on a flaky node and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`? also `sudo iptables -t nat -S` to see NAT chains.
maria: ran checks: `conntrack` count 65536, `nf_conntrack_max=65536`. iptables nat shows a `REDIRECT` from OUTPUT to ENVOY_EGRESS and a custom chain `EDGE_EGRESS` inserted before `POSTROUTING`.
maria: also noticed envoy is returning `503 upstream connect error` to several external hosts while raw curl on host with `--net=host` works. curl from pod fails.
ankit: if traffic is redirected into envoy but SNAT still done post-postrouting, we could be double-proxying and depleting ephemeral ports.
joel: quick mitigation: revert the redirect and let egress-gateway handle allowed hosts only. can someone roll back the iptables change?
olivia: rolling back mesh redirect on 3 affected nodepools now (kube daemonset patch). will monitor. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rollback of iptables-redirect applied to edge-np-eu-west1 at 08:39 UTC by olivia (change-id: chg-3321).
maria: after rollback, `conntrack` dropped to ~18k within 2m and model pulls resumed. metrics sink backlog cleared.
ankit: root cause summary: aggressive PREROUTING redirect of all outbound HTTPS into the sidecar caused large number of short-lived proxied connections -> conntrack table exhaustion and ICMP errors. we intended host-based allowlist but the redirect was too broad.
joel: action items: 1) tighten redirect to only egress-gateway traffic hosts; 2) add conntrack alert (threshold 50k) and dashboard; 3) document safe SNAT + envoy routing pattern for edge nodepools.
maria: also adding a rule to bypass envoy for node-local metadata and registry IPs (169.254.169.254 and model-registry CIDRs) so health checks and long-lived pulls don't go through proxy.
ankit: will push a smaller change to the mesh config with explicit host allowlist and a note to ops to scale `nf_conntrack_max` on older node images as temporary buffer.
olivia: opened PR with the restricted redirect and bypass list: https://git.company/redwood/infra/merge/2345.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-045 (egress-proxy-conntrack-exhaustion). severity: p2.
maria: thanks all — marking this thread resolved for now. will follow up with postmortem and checklist for sidecar egress rollouts. :memo:
